recipes.name: Mackerel Fish Curry with Coconut Milk
recipes.health_benefit: Rich in Omega-3 fatty acids, which may help improve HDL levels and manage triglycerides. Lean protein supports overall health.
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and curry leaves; let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and mushy.
Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Cook for 2-3 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed to prevent burning.
Add the mackerel pieces and gently mix with the masala.
Pour in the coconut milk and 1/2 cup of water. Add salt to taste. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until fish is cooked through. Do not overcook.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: Palak Dal (Spinach Lentil Curry)
recipes.health_benefit: Excellent source of fiber, which helps manage blood glucose and cholesterol. Spinach provides iron, supporting hemoglobin levels.
instructions: Wash masoor dal thoroughly and soak for 15-20 minutes. Drain.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker or pot. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato and cook until soft.
Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Cook for a minute.
Add the drained dal and chopped spinach. Mix well.
Pour in 2-3 cups of water. For a pressure cooker, cook for 3-4 whistles. For a pot, simmer until dal is soft.
Mash lightly with the back of a spoon if a smoother consistency is desired. Serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Ragi Dosa with Sambhar
recipes.prep_time: 15 mins (plus soaking/fermentation time for dosa batter)
recipes.health_benefit: Ragi (finger millet) is an excellent dairy-free source of calcium and fiber, supporting bone health and blood sugar management. Sambhar provides fiber and plant-based protein.
instructions: For Dosa: Mix ragi flour, rice flour, and salt with water to form a smooth batter of pouring consistency. Let it rest for 15-30 minutes (or ferment overnight if desired for a sour taste).
Heat a non-stick tawa. Pour a ladleful of batter and spread it thinly in a circular motion.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until golden brown and crisp on both sides. Repeat for remaining batter.
For Sambhar: Cook arhar dal with turmeric until soft. Keep aside.
In a separate pan, heat a little oil. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add tomato and cook until soft.
Add mixed vegetables, sambhar powder, and tamarind pulp. Add some water and cook until vegetables are tender.
Add the cooked dal to the vegetable mixture. Mix well, adjust consistency with water if needed, and bring to a simmer for 5-7 minutes. Serve hot with Ragi Dosa.

recipes.name: Chicken and Spinach Stir-fry (Palak Chicken)
recipes.health_benefit: Provides lean protein for muscle health and satiety. Spinach contributes iron for hemoglobin and essential vitamins. This dish is low in unhealthy fats, supporting triglyceride and cholesterol management.
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a large pan or wok. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add sliced onion and sauté until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and cook until they turn white and are lightly browned.
Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add sliced bell pepper and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Add chopped spinach and cook until it wilts completely. Do not overcook to retain nutrients.
Stir in garam masala and mix well. Check seasoning.
Serve hot with whole wheat roti or brown rice.

recipes.name: Oats Daliya with Berries and Flaxseeds (Dairy-Free)
recipes.health_benefit: High in soluble fiber, which can help lower LDL cholesterol and regulate blood sugar. Flaxseeds provide Omega-3s and fiber, beneficial for heart health and triglycerides. Berries add antioxidants and vitamins.
instructions: In a saucepan, combine rolled oats and fortified oat milk. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oats are cooked and the daliya has thickened to your desired consistency.
Remove from heat. Stir in ground flaxseeds.
Transfer to a bowl. Top with mixed berries and chopped almonds.
Add maple syrup or jaggery powder if desired. Serve warm.

recipes.name: Egg Bhurji (Scrambled Eggs) with Whole Wheat Toast
recipes.health_benefit: Eggs are a complete protein source and provide Vitamin B12 and Vitamin D (if fortified). This dish offers a lean, satisfying breakfast that contributes to daily protein and vitamin targets.
instructions: Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt, turmeric powder, and red chili powder in a bowl.
Heat groundnut oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add green chili (if using).
Add chopped tomato and cook until it softens.
Pour in the whisked eggs. Let it set slightly, then gently scramble with a spatula.
Cook until the eggs are firm but still moist. Stir in chopped coriander leaves.
Toast the whole wheat bread slices.
Serve the hot egg bhurji with whole wheat toast.

recipes.name: Brown Rice Pulao with Tofu and Mixed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: Brown rice provides complex carbohydrates and fiber, aiding blood sugar and cholesterol management. Tofu is a dairy-free protein source, and mixed vegetables add essential vitamins, minerals, and fiber.

ingredients.item: Mixed vegetables (carrots, peas, beans, bell peppers)

instructions: Rinse brown rice thoroughly and soak for at least 30 minutes, then drain.
Heat mustard oil in a pot or pressure cooker. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods. Let them splutter.
Add sliced onion and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for 1 minute.
Add cubed tofu and cook until lightly browned. Remove from pot and set aside.
Add mixed vegetables to the same pot and sauté for 3-4 minutes.
Add the soaked brown rice, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix gently.
Pour in 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes (or 2 whistles in a pressure cooker) until rice is cooked and water is absorbed.
Once cooked, gently fluff the rice with a fork. Stir in the browned tofu and fresh coriander leaves.
Serve hot.
